title: Ostrobothnia: 1.1 more lung cancer patients a year treated to cure, for €47,900 a year
markdown:
# Ostrobothnia: 1.1 more lung cancer patients a year treated to cure, for €47,900 a year

> 1.1 more patients a year treated to cure · €47,900 of €1.00M · €952,100 left: nothing else pays off at these assumptions

## The gap

Of 100 lung cancer patients in Ostrobothnia, 28 get treatment that aims to cure. In Finland it is 27. The difference is within what chance alone gives a county of this size. [^care_curative] Compared with the best quarter of counties (30.4%), about 2.3 patients a year are missing from treatment that aims to cure, range 0.0–6.0 [^care_curative] [^model]. Against Finland as a whole, there is no measured shortfall to split between operations and radiotherapy (range 0.0–3.0 patients a year) [^model].

## The target

Raise the share of lung cancer patients treated to cure from 27.8% to 29.0% by 2028: 1.1 more patients a year (range 0.0–1.1), for €47,900 a year, about €45,189 per extra patient. [^care_curative][^model]

## Funded actions

| # | Action and owner | Cost a year | More patients treated to cure a year (range) | First step this week | Measure: today → target |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| | **The county can start on Monday** | | | | |
| 1 | **Precise radiotherapy (SBRT) for early cancer in patients who cannot be operated**[^ev_sbrt_pathway_1]. Chief physician of oncology; chief of radiotherapy at the university hospital | €19,960 | 0.7 (0.0–0.9) | Write the referral rule: every stage I patient not accepted for surgery is referred for stereotactic radiotherapy the same week. | Share of patients who get treatment that aims to cure: 27.8% → 28.6% by 2028 |
| 2 | **Travel and hotel paid for patients far from the university hospital**[^ev_travel_accommodation_support_1]. Chief physician of oncology and hospital social work; university hospital patient hotel | €27,940 | 0.4 (0.0–0.3) | Name one contact person who books the patient hotel and transport for every patient sent to the university hospital for curative treatment. | Share of patients who get treatment that aims to cure: 27.8% → 28.2% by 2028 |
| | **Total** | **€47,900** | **1.1 (0.0–1.1)** | | |

No trial has measured these effects; the low end of every range is zero. The ranges do not add up to the range of the total, because the measures share one ceiling. Costs are assumptions. [^model]

## Needs a national decision (outside this budget)

- **Low-dose CT screening for long-term heavy smokers**[^ev_ldct_screening_1]: Ministry of Social Affairs and Health and Palko (decision), Finnish Cancer Registry (steering), county (delivery). €558,665 a year; modelled to avoid 1.0 deaths a year (0.2–2.5). Not counted in this budget. Not a county decision. Ask the Ministry and Palko for the timetable after the 2026-2028 pilot and offer the county as a pilot site. [^model]

## What to measure from Monday

- Share of patients treated to cure: 27.8% (2019–2023, measured) → 29.0% by 2028. [^care_curative][^model]
- The registry's public figures cover 2019–2023; count these each month from the county's own records. [^care_curative]

## What more money buys, and what it cannot

€47,900 buys every measure that adds patients treated to cure in Ostrobothnia [^model]. The remaining €952,100 buys nothing more in the model, because these measures are limited by the reachable part of the measured shortfall, not by money [^model]. Other uses for the money are low-dose CT screening for long-term heavy smokers, which needs a national decision, or ranking measures by deaths avoided [^model]. Lung cancer causes 70.4 deaths a year here, and this plan is modelled to avoid 0.2 of them (range 0.0–0.34) [^deaths] [^model].

## Limits

- Effects are assumptions that no trial has measured. The range runs from all lowest to all highest values together and is not a probability [^model].
- Shares are adjusted only for residents' age, not for stage at diagnosis, other illness, histology or smoking. County figures cannot show cause [^model].
- In a check, 0 of 3 measured outcomes matched the estimated symptom-to-treatment clock beyond chance [^model].

removed.reason: The source does not state that the plan does not use the clock; it only calls the clock a secondary, estimated view. The following sentence was minimally reworded so it names the clock instead of referring back with 'it'.

flagged.sentence: €47,900 buys every measure that adds patients treated to cure in Ostrobothnia.
flagged.reason: The figure had no source marker. The supporting id is plainly the model (plan.saturation_note), so [^model] was added.

flagged.sentence: The remaining €952,100 buys nothing more, because these measures are limited by the reachable part of the measured shortfall, not by money [^model].
flagged.reason: This is a model result stated as fact. 'In the model' was added, as in the source saturation note.

flagged.sentence: More could come from low-dose CT screening for long-term heavy smokers, which needs a national decision, or from ranking measures by deaths avoided [^model].
flagged.reason: The source gives no estimate showing these would add more patients treated to cure. It only points to them as other uses of the money, so the sentence was reworded to 'Other uses for the money are…'.
